## About

Artificial intelligence is now deeply embedded in everyday life and represents a transformative force for society. This program equips students with both foundational principles and advanced methodologies in AI, enabling them to become technical leaders in this rapidly evolving field.

The curriculum offers a distinctive approach by integrating model- and symbolic-driven methods with data-driven artificial intelligence techniques. Students explore how these approaches apply to critical societal domains, including sustainable development, new mobility systems, network infrastructures, Industry 4.0, finance, and health and well-being.

Delivered entirely in English by leading academics and industry professionals, the program provides a comprehensive end-to-end learning experience—from theory to real-world implementation. It is designed for students aiming to become AI architects and innovators, offering outstanding career prospects in one of the most dynamic and impactful disciplines of the 21st century.

The MSc in AI Applied to Society is officially certified and registered in the Répertoire National des Certifications Professionnelles (RNCP) by CentraleSupélec and the French Ministry of Higher Education and Research (Level 7 qualification).

## Program

Artificial Intelligence is a dynamic field at the intersection of science and technology, developed to solve complex problems that require intelligent, adaptive solutions. Since its formal emergence in 1956, AI has advanced at an extraordinary pace, transforming industries and reshaping societies worldwide. By joining the MSc in Artificial Intelligence at CentraleSupélec, you will acquire the expertise needed to contribute to the responsible development of this transformative technology and help shape the future.

In a world increasingly shaped by AI, the program provides rigorous scientific training focused on innovation and societal impact. It addresses major economic, environmental, medical, industrial, and financial challenges, equipping students with both advanced technical competencies and a strong understanding of real-world applications.

### M1 Program

Basic Science

* UE 1 : Basics in Mathematic & Optimization
* UE 2 : Python Programming and Data Science
* UE 3 : Probability & Statistics
* UE 4 : Foundation of Machine Learning
* UE 5 : Model Representation and Analysis

Hands-On Learning

* Industrial conference on the use of AI
* Workshop on improving public speaking skills
* Project management workshop
* Capstone Project: AI for Real-World physical systems
* Innovation project: Cross-lab thematic research project
* Advanced Applied Project

Professional & International Development

* UE : Risks and responsabilities of AI
* Foreign languages
* Culture
* Internship : 3 months minimum

### M2 Program

The M2 program is structured into three phases:

1. Core courses provide fundamental and advanced knowledge of AI.
2. Elective courses that allow specialization, conducted in parallel with a laboratory research project.
3. A professional internship culminating in a Master’s thesis.

This structure ensures a comprehensive learning journey from theoretical foundations to applied research and professional practice.

Artificial Intelligence now impacts every sector of society. At CentraleSupélec, five specialized tracks allow you to explore how AI drives innovation in sustainable energy, healthcare/biomedical, transportation/mobility, industry of the future, and AI for finance—preparing you to design high-impact solutions for tomorrow’s challenges.

* ### 

  Renewable energy plays a huge part in the building of a better future, and Artificial Intelligence is a fundamental building block of the clean energy transition: contributing to the improvement and acceleration of the energy industry; improving our ability to understand and forecast energy demand; managing network infrastructures; and sustainably managing natural resources in a balanced way.

  We face a further challenge as we strive to make Artificial intelligence energy efficient by optimizing AI architectures to balance efficiency and energy consumption.
* ### 

  Transportation accounts for a large part of energy consumption. Private cars are a major source of pollution. Transitioning to new forms of shared / sustainable mobility poses a considerable challenge. Artificial intelligence has a major contribution to make to the mobility revolution, particularly in the future of multimodal urban mobility.

  Crucial areas include designing resilient public transport networks, addressing road safety for autonomous vehicles, predicting traffic flows to minimize congestion, and using AI for transport operations planning/regulation and asset management.
* ### 

  Artificial intelligence is a powerful lever for improving medicine and healthcare. The benefits of Artificial Intelligence in medicine and health are everywhere to be seen: improved pathology detection and diagnosis; personalized medicine; informed patient care; and better organized healthcare systems.

  AI technologies and methods have already proven successful across a variety of health applications, and the potential for further progress is enormous.

  In this sector, more than in others, Artificial intelligence designers face ethical questions about the respect for private data.
* ### 

  Digital, physical and virtual worlds generate massive shifts across industries. Artificial intelligence is central to this revolution. Typical examples of how Artificial intelligence contributes to industry transformation include predictive maintenance, digital twins and robotics.

  The industrial systems of the future will involve collaboration between human operators and software agents, with the two working together (man-machine teaming). The challenges of this field of application require trustworthy, safe, robust, and explainable AI to design industrial systems of the future that are driven by humans.
* ### 

  Finance is one of the most data-intensive sectors in the modern world and is constantly evolving. Artificial intelligence is transforming financial services, enabling reassuring governance, relevant and intelligent decision-making, and real-time risk management, thereby refining the customer experience. It also supports the design of sustainable financial models grounded in fundamentals and helps assess the environmental impact of investments, contributing to the development of responsible financial strategies. At the same time, artificial intelligence raises crucial questions of transparency, explicability and fairness, particularly when algorithms can influence credit assessment or investment decisions. AI for Finance: to be at the forefront of tomorrow’s responsible and innovative financial systems.

  ##### (September to December)

  + ### 

    Machine learning is the scientific field that provides computers with the ability to learn without being explicitly programmed. Machine learning lies at the heart of many real-world applications, including recommender systems, web search, computer vision, autonomous cars, and automatic language translation.

    The course will provide an overview of fundamental topics and important trends in machine learning, including algorithms for supervised and unsupervised learning, dimensionality reduction methods, and their applications. A substantial lab section will involve group projects for a data science competition and will allow students to apply the course theory to real-world problems.
  + ### 

    Optimization is the body of mathematical techniques at the root of all modern machine learning methods. Although these methods are quite varied, they can all be formulated as the minimization of a cost function over a given domain, subject to constraints. Nonetheless, formulating a minimization problem is only a starting point. Indeed, many existing optimization methods depend on the structure of the issue at hand, some more efficient than others. This course aims to provide a comprehensive overview of classical optimization approaches and algorithms, both discrete and continuous. Participants will learn to address the various optimization problems they may encounter in practice and to choose an appropriate algorithm.

    The lecture will cover local and global optimization methods. The topics will include discrete, derivative-free optimization, gradient, and second-order based algorithms, constrained optimization, duality, non-smooth methods, and an introduction to stochastic and global algorithms. The course will use machine-learning methods as illustrations but occasionally draw on other examples.
  + ### 

    Big data is a generic term for large datasets that are so large and complex that traditional data-processing methods cannot handle them. These are typically impossible to store on any single computer, no matter how powerful. For example, think of the collection of web pages of the entire Internet; all the medical exams of the whole healthcare system in France or the USA; or the collision data from the Large Hadron Collider in Geneva. Somewhat smaller datasets are daunting too: the catalog of auto parts for all cars on the road today, for example, or the collection of photos on Facebook (estimated at 50 billion). One estimates that the entire Internet traffic is in the order of one zettabyte per year (1021 bytes) and doubling every year.

    In this course, we will introduce state-of-the-art techniques for distributed data processing, with a particular focus on Apache Spark and its high-level libraries for handling (semi-)structured, streaming, and graph data.

    We’ll also cover the MLlib library that Spark provides for training, testing, and deploying machine learning models at scale.
  + ### 

    Deep Learning is becoming increasingly popular, with algorithms based on these techniques performing very well across a variety of problems and scientific communities. The course has been designed to provide an introduction to deep learning techniques, including neural networks, computer vision, and natural image processing. In particular, it will cover the fundamental aspects and recent developments in deep learning: Feedforward networks and their optimization and regularization, representation learning and siamese networks, Generative Adversarial Networks and transfer learning, recurrent networks and Long Short Term Memory units.
  + ### 

    Artificial Intelligence is experiencing another hype phase, driven by massive funding from private companies. The history of this fascinating scientific field shows it is not the first hype phase, and probably not the last one. The course is an opportunity to understand better the history of IA, its founding fathers, and the great names in this field.

    It is an overview of the different approaches to Artificial Intelligence: from reflex agents (low-level AI) to expert systems and xIA (high-level AI). It will show various categories of problems AI can solve. Each approach will be illustrated with real-world applications.

    The course will provide an overview of fundamental topics and important trends in machine learning, including algorithms for supervised and unsupervised learning, as well as dimensionality reduction methods and their applications. A substantial lab section will involve group projects for a data science competition and will give students the ability to apply the course theory to real-world problems.
  + ### 

    Preferences are present and pervasive in many situations involving human interaction and decisions.Preferences are expressed explicitly or implicitly across numerous applications, and relevant decisions should be made based on them. This course aims to introduce preference models for multicriteria decision-making. We will present concepts and methods for preference modelling and multicriteria decision-making.
  + ### 

    In these two sessions, we will tackle a key question: what can go wrong when implementing new technologies, and AI in particular? Building on numerous examples from the peer-reviewed literature, we will explore aspects that require attention when developing, calibrating, testing, and deploying AI-based tools.

    The first lecture will introduce ethical issues: biases, responsibility, privacy, and sustainability. From a human factors/ergonomics perspective, the second lecture will show how failing to consider AI as one element of a larger system can lead to unexpected consequences.

  ##### (December to April)

  + ### 

    This course will provide an overview of the field of Natural Language Processing.It will take a problem-centric approach, introducing increasingly complex problems, starting with fundamental building blocks such as language modelling, tagging, and parsing, and progressing to more advanced areas such as opinion mining, machine translation, question & answering, and dialogue. While critical historical methods will be mentioned (and studied if still relevant), a focus will be on current state-of-the-art, including many recent advances in neural network training and novel architectures.
  + ### 

    Computer vision is an interdisciplinary field that aims to enable the automatic processing and understanding of digital images. These images can be captured by video cameras, radars, satellites, or even very specialised sensors such as those used for medical purposes. This course covers both theoretical and practical aspects of computer vision. It has been designed to provide an introduction to computer vision, including fundamentals on image processing, computational photography, multiview geometry, stereo, tracking, segmentation and object detection. It will expose students to several real-world applications that are important to our daily lives. The course will focus solely on classical computer vision techniques, providing a detailed overview of classical methods, but it does not cover deep learning-based methods.
  + ### 

    Reinforcement Learning (RL) methods lie at the intersection of several fields, including machine learning, probability theory, control theory, and game theory. They study fundamental trade-offs between exploitation and exploration to optimise future rewards in an unknown environment. Recently, they were successfully applied to many applications, such as complex games (Go or Atari), robot control, and expert selection, leading, in many cases, to superhuman performance in those contexts. This class will cover the necessary tools (both theoretical and practical) to understand how such a breakthrough was possible.
  + ### 

    Deep learning methods are now state-of-the-art across many machine learning tasks, yielding impressive results. Nevertheless, neural networks are still poorly understood, neural network training is still tricky, and the results are black boxes lacking explanations. Given the societal impact of machine learning techniques today (used for medical assistance, hiring processes, and bank loans…), it is crucial to make their decisions explainable or to offer guarantees. Besides, real-world problems usually do not fit the standard assumptions or frameworks of the most famous academic work (data quantity and quality, availability of expert knowledge…). This course aims to provide insights and tools to address these practical aspects, grounded in mathematical concepts.
  + ### 

    Networks (or graphs) have become ubiquitous as data from diverse disciplines can naturally be mapped to graph structures. Social networks, such as academic collaboration networks and interaction networks over online social networking applications are used to represent and model social ties among individuals. Information networks, including the hyperlink structure of the Web and blog networks, have become crucial media for information dissemination, offering an effective way to represent and navigate content. A plethora of technological networks, including the Internet, power grids, telephone networks, and road networks, are essential to everyday life. The problem of efficiently and effectively extracting meaningful information from large-scale graph data has become crucial and challenging across several essential applications. Towards this end, graph mining and analysis methods constitute prominent tools. The goal of this course is to present recent, state-of-the-art techniques and algorithms for analysing, mining, and learning large-scale graph data, as well as their practical applications across various domains (e.g., the web, social networks, recommender systems).
  + ### 

    Medical imaging technologies provide unparalleled means to study the structure and function of the human body in vivo. Interpretation of medical images is difficult because it requires accounting for three-dimensional, time-varying information across multiple image types. Artificial intelligence (AI) holds great promise for assisting in interpretation, and medical imaging is one of the areas where AI is expected to yield the most significant successes. In the past years, deep learning technologies have led to impressive advances in medical image processing and interpretation. This course covers both theoretical and practical aspects of deep learning for medical imaging. It covers the main tasks in medical image analysis (classification, segmentation, registration, and generative models). It presents state-of-the-art deep learning techniques alongside more traditional image processing and machine learning approaches. Examples of differenttypes of medical imaging applications (brain, cardiac…) will also be provided.
  + ### 

    Ensemble methods are popular machine learning techniques that are powerful for both classification and regression. The idea is to build a global prediction model by combining the strengths of a set of simpler base models. The random Forests approach is an example that falls into this category by aggregating a collection of decision trees.

    This course aims to study the fundamental notions and concepts of tree-based methods and ensemble learning. We will mainly introduce several methods, such as Classification and Regression Trees (CART), boosting trees, and Random Forests. Furthermore, we want to investigate and discuss recent challenges in interpretability and regularisation using different approaches [Strobl et al., 2007, 2008]. Moreover, the various methods will be applied to practical cases involving real data throughout the course.
  + ### 

    Multi-agent systems (MAS) are widely used, especially for complex applications that require interaction among several entities. More specifically, they are used in applications where it is necessary to solve problems in a distributed manner (e.g., data processing) or in the design of distributed systems in which each component has some degree of autonomy (e.g., process control). Examples of applications include trading agents, drones, and smart grids. This course will begin with an introduction to agents and multi-agent systems. It will present the concepts that will lead to an understanding of what an agent is and how it can be built. Then, we will address a classical problem in SMAs: how to model and simulate a situation using the concept of agents.The idea is to provide a basis for understanding how agent-based simulations can be used as tools for understanding human societies and complex problems and situations. Besides, we will discuss how agents can communicate and interact to solve problems, and more specifically, to make noncentralized decisions. For this, we will rely on negotiation protocols based on argumentation theory, a process of constructing and evaluating arguments (positive and negative reasons/evidence) to resolve conflicts.
  + ### 

    Maintenance is essential in engineering systems. In this course, we focus on the optimal planning of maintenance for complex systems. Different maintenance strategies are introduced with a focus on the performance indicators used to quantify their performance and optimization models used to obtain optimal planning. The students are supposed to learn fundamental theoretical results as well as tools to help them apply theoretical methods in practice.
  + ### 

    Planning in AI focuses on automatically generating sequences of actions to reach a predefined goal. Actions are represented by operators that transform states, generally expressed in propositional logic. Several problems in industry or robotics can be formulated as planning issues. Different AI techniques and algorithms are used to solve planning problems. In classical planning, an agent has perfect knowledge of the states and the effects of the actions, which are deterministic. The relaxation of these assumptions leads to numerous extensions that use solving techniques based on diverse AI tools, such as heuristic search or Markov processes.

    In this course, we will introduce the formulation of a planning problem and present the different AI techniques and algorithms for solving it.
  + ### 

    Artificial Intelligence aims to solve problems automatically. In particular, Deep Learning enables achieving performance levels often exceeding human performance. However, in some application areas, users want to understand why an algorithm proposes a specific decision. This is especially true for human-centred domains, such as medicine and security, or for those affected by laws granting a right to explanation (the banking sector). For these reasons, the field of XAI (eXplainable Artificial Intelligence) has become very important in recent years, even though the issue has been around for several decades.This module aims to introduce you to tools that have emerged from recent or older research to help you understand the most opaque models and to familiarise you with interpretability and explainability issues. At the end of this course, the student will have acquired a general view of the XIA domain and its problems.
  + ### 

    Decision-making is an indispensable task in engineering practices. In this course, we focus on the basic concepts, principles, and decision-making techniques using optimization models, especially in the presence of uncertainties.

    The students are supposed to learn to model optimization problems involving risk and uncertainty using analytical models and off-the-shelf software. The course covers analytical models such as the basics of Convex Optimisation, Stochastic Programming, Risk Control in Stochastic Optimisation, Two-stage Stochastic Programming, Decomposition algorithms, Markov Decision Process, and Dynamic Programming. The course is hands-on. The emphasis will be on model formulation, practical problem-solving, implementation, and interpretation of results.
  + ### 

    Artificial intelligence cannot be applied straightforwardly to finance for three essential reasons: data are extremely noisy, their distributions are usually far more non-Gaussian, and everything is nonstationary. These basic facts of life in finance, therefore, require special care, that is, specific methodologies and expertise.

    This course aims at giving a practical approach to applying AI to finance: starting from fundamental concepts and objects, it then explores price formation in high-frequency data in limit order books, introduces modern methods of portfolio optimization, explains the good practices of trading strategy performance backtesting, and finally reviews what kind of DL/ML/RL approaches work in finance.

  ##### (October to March)

  Students, working in pairs, select a research topic under the supervision of a faculty member in an associated laboratory. The topic corresponds to a state-of-the-art problem. Students are asked to assess the existing literature, propose an algorithmic solution to the issue at hand, implement it, and provide numerical validation

  + ### 

    To complete the CentraleSupélec MSc in Artificial Intelligence, students must acquire professional experience (by means of a 4-6 month internship or a job in a position related to the program) and complete the related Master’s Thesis. This corresponds to a natural extension of the coursework carried out during the academic year

Optimization for Machine Learning

**Publications:** [Profile](https://www.centralesupelec.fr/chercheurs/hugues-talbot)

Multi Agent Systems

Assistant Professor in Computer Science at CentraleSupélec and a member of the MICS Lab. She holds a PhD in Computer Science from the University of Paris Dauphine in 2009.

Her research is related to Knowledge Representation and Reasoning within the context of Explainable AI, with the aim of using formal tools from AI and decision theory to specify agent reasoning (resolving conflicts, explaining decisions, etc.) and facilitate agent communication (dialogue protocol).

**Publications:** [Profile](https://www.centralesupelec.fr/chercheurs/wassila-ouerdane)

Network Science Analytics

Assistant Professor at CentraleSupélec and an associate researcher at Inria Saclay (OPIS team). He was a postdoctoral researcher at UC San Diego (2016-17) and École Polytechnique (2015-2016) where he received his PhD in Computer Science in 2015.

His research interests span the broad field of data science, focusing on graph machine learning and graph-based information extraction.

**Publications:** [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=_7heOKcAAAAJ&hl=en&oi=sra)

Foundations of Artificial Intelligence

Senior expert in Artificial Intelligence at CEA-LIST. He received his PhD from Aix-Marseille Université and the Institut National de l’Audiovisuel in 2007 on the automatic structuring of television streams.

His research concerns symbolic Artificial Intelligence, in particular symbolic machine learning and eXplainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI).

**Publications:** [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.fr/citations?user=Ce3Ew_YAAAAJ)

### Frédéric Pascal

Advanced Statistics

Full Professor in AI at the L2S lab at CentraleSupélec, University Paris-Saclay. Since December 2019 he is the director of the AI@CS Hub coordinating artificial intelligence activities.

He is also the Givaudan chair in data sciences and has been part of the executive committee of the DATAIA institute, where he later became Co-Director and VP for AI at University Paris-Saclay.

**Publications:** [Profile](https://www.centralesupelec.fr/chercheurs/frederic-pascal)

### Damien Challet

Artificial Intelligence for Finance

Damien Challet obtained his PhD in Theoretical Physics from Université de Fribourg in 2000. He joined the MICS lab at CentraleSupélec in 2011 where he is now full professor.

His research interests include agent-based modelling, statistical learning, cognitive biases, market microstructure, and large-scale human-made systems.

**Publications:** [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=63f3FggAAAAJ&hl=en)

### Laurence Carassus

Artificial Intelligence for Finance

Graduated from Paris-Dauphine University with a Master’s degree in Applied Mathematics and a Master’s Degree in Audit. She also holds a PhD and an HDR in Applied Mathematics.

Her work focuses on probability applied to finance and mathematical economics, particularly incomplete markets, with publications in leading journals.

**Publications:** [Profile](https://www.centralesupelec.fr/chercheurs/laurence-carassus)

![Ioane Muni Toke](/sites/default/files/centralesupelec/images/photos/ioane-muni-toke.png)

### Ioane Muni Toke

Artificial Intelligence for Finance

Associate Professor at CentraleSupélec, Université Paris-Saclay. He previously worked at the University of Texas at Dallas and the University of New Caledonia.

His research focuses on probability and statistics applied to quantitative finance, especially financial market microstructure and limit order books.

**Publications:** [Profile](https://www.centralesupelec.fr/chercheurs/ioane-muni-toke)

Located within the world-class ecosystem of Université Paris-Saclay, the CentraleSupélec campus in Paris-Saclay offers an environment where Artificial Intelligence is not simply taught — it is actively developed, deployed, and researched at scale.

## Summer Research Exchange: CentraleSupelec

[CentraleSupélec](https://www.centralesupelec.fr/en) is a public institution under ministerial charter, devoted to the sciences and engineering. This charter is shared between the Ministry of Higher Education, Research and Innovation, and the Ministry of Economy, Industry and Digital Technologies.

CentraleSupélec was officially established on January 1st, 2015, bringing together two leading engineering schools in France; Ecole Centrale Paris and Supélec. The co-operation between our two *grandes écoles*, as they are known in the French system, had progressively been gaining momentum since 2009, with sustained alliance in three core areas: engineering education, executive education and research.

More information about [CentraleSupelec](https://learningabroad.utoronto.ca/wp-content/uploads/Presentation_CS_UofT.pdf)

## Program

* ### 

  An intelligent use of data nowadays forms the core of business decisions constitutes the driving force of the societal and economic evolution of the years to come. It is probably one of the most important topics of our days. Analysts estimate that data-related businesses generated about 10 billion dollars in recent years, and will probably generate more than 30 billion dollars in the years to come.

  **The growth in job opportunities is tremendous**: companies and organizations will need a couple of hundred thousand data scientists and business analytics leaders in the next few years. Moreover, the exponential growth in content-generation will bring about a huge need for highly qualified individuals with an **in-depth knowledge and a global understanding** of the technological and business challenges underlying the AI and digital revolution era.

  Recent business studies converge to an estimated need of educating several million data scientists and leaders within the decade to come. This is why two prestigious French Grandes Ecoles ESSEC Business School and CentraleSupélec have partnered to propose this very innovative and complete program. We believe **that truly innovative leaders must be both business savvy and erudite in data sciences**. Hence we propose a unique program where students learn and combine the key skills in innovation and wealth creation that companies will increasingly require.

  This master is for students who are committed to a deep understanding of data sciences and the methods of business analytics, who aim to develop strong skills in mathematical modeling and computer science as well as management savviness.
* ### 

  This hybrid program combines faculty resources of a Top Business School and a Top Engineering School, in Paris and Singapore, to provide a unique and innovative 2-year program (M1+M2) or 1-year program (M2 only), depending on your previous degree and background.

  **Our promise to future students is that you will**:

  + Gain a deep understanding of scientific models and methods.
  + Boost your imagination, creativity and critical thinking.
  + Lead changes in business practices, technologies and tools
  + Succeed in managing complex projects.

  ### What Makes this Program Unique?

  For a global understanding of the challenges underlying the digital era and to master the science of data and the techniques of business analytics, the program has a strong scientific focus and aims to provide students with a comprehensive view of these complementary and intrinsically linked fields, enabling them to develop as fully-operational professionals.

* ###

  If you have or are currently pursuing:  
  - A 3-year Bachelor or a Licence 3 at the minimum: you will complete the program in 2 years (M1+M2).  
  - A 4-year Bachelor or a Master Degree at the minimum: you will complete the program in 1 year (M2).  
  If the commission board finds that your background is strong but not complete enough in some required aspects, we may ask you to join the two-year program (M1+M2) instead in order to build up your strength and ensure your success.

## Combine the power of three campuses

Choosing the MSc in Data Sciences & Business Analytics means you will enjoy studying at up to three campuses. Two of these are around Paris, France, the third in Singapore. Regardless of your campus choice, however, you are sure to pursue your degree in a spacious, conducive environment for you to reach your highest potential.

* ### 

  At just 35 minutes from the bustling business district La Défense, stands the iconic ESSEC France Campus. Located in the second largest student area in Ile-de-France, housing over 27,000 students, the France campus provides everything you need to develop and enjoy your academic career to the fullest.

  The campus is a very modern home to our 4000 students: they use the latest technologies in our Knowledge Labs, enjoy a nice meal together in restaurant The Daily Market and of course relax and socialize in the Foy’s bar. Our students are very diverse and active: there are over 100 student associations you can join.

  Most importantly, however, next to great facilities and modern infrastructures, the ESSEC France campus is renowned for the power of its programs. Expect nothing short of top-of-the-bill educational programs provided by the world’s best professors. Your development won’t stop at the classroom door either: 1500 managers yearly come and recruit our students during events. Next to that, at the ESSEC France campus, we have our very own two incubators at the heart of our entrepreneurial ecosystem. In other words: you can directly put your most creative and innovative ideas to the test, do internships and apprenticeships at world-changing companies of France, while immersed in the rich French culture (and pick up French, while you’re at it…!)
* ### 

  In September 2017, CentraleSupélec will open the doors to its brand new Saclay campus, in Gif-sur-Yvette: 105,000m2 of excellence and innovation comprising 4 buildings, of which two are completely new. This will facilitate exchange and interdisciplinarity.

  Significant joint equipment (student accommodation, a learning center, library, gym, sports courts, etc.) will be added to this which, along with ENS Paris-Saclay and Paris-Sud University, will ultimately make up the largest district of the Saclay Plateau: the Moulon district. Located 25 km south of Paris, it will attract more than 30,000 people, of which 8,000 students and scientific equipment employees from both public and private sectors.

  On this campus, we bring over 2,000 students from 60 countries together. They all manage their cultural, social and even technological activities there. Activities such as Gala, Central Business Forum, Centrale 7, and so on. Doing sports and relaxing is also essential for many Centralers’: our campus houses gyms, restaurants, collaborative work spaces, sports rooms and many other facilities. Studying here, you can enjoy an intense and convivial student life!

  Proudly representing South-East Asia, one of the most dynamic, fast-growing and economically promising parts of the world, is the Republic of Singapore: home to a booming technology sector, a startup ecology that’s picking up strength and speed, and a few of the most advanced cities in the world. ESSEC Business School and CentraleSupelec have joined forces to create an international Bachelor program in Artificial Intelligence, Data and Management Sciences. Information technologies, and in particular massive data processing and artificial intelligence, are a source of both opportunities and challenges for organizations and societies.

It is essential that the young generation understands the dynamics of the current transitions, strongly affected by the social, environmental and digital transformations of society, and be properly equipped to handled them.

  CentraleSupélec has an exceptional campus on the **Saclay Plateau**, in Gif-sur-Yvette: 105,000 m² of excellence and innovation comprising 3 new buildings. This will facilitate exchange and interdisciplinarity.

Your development won’t stop at the classroom door either: 1500 managers yearly come and recruit our students during events. Next to that, at the ESSEC France campus, we have our very own two incubators at the heart of our entrepreneurial ecosystem. In other words: you can directly put your most creative and innovative ideas to the test, do internships and apprenticeships at world-changing companies of France, while immersed in the rich French culture (and pick up French, while you’re at it…!)
